findings.spec: FR-13 / Flow 3 step 3: the digest links to the owner's approval inbox, which is one page per location
findings.summary: digestEmail and lowRatingEmail link every location's email to /inbox. /inbox takes the location only from the session cookie (src/app/inbox/route.ts), and an owner session covers one location. For a business with two or more locations, an owner signed in to location A who opens location B's digest or low-rating email sees A's inbox, without B's waiting drafts.
findings.verification: code trace: ownerEmails.ts inboxUrl() ignores the location; ownerEmails.test.ts asserts the exact URL `${BASE}/inbox`; /inbox reads only the cookie; /account/inbox/[locationId] is POST-only, so no per-location GET link exists to point at
findings.reason_not_fixed: a correct link needs a per-location entry URL (for example a GET /account/inbox/<locationId> that switches the session, or /account for multi-location businesses), which is the open entry-point decision D-2. Pilots are single-location, where the link is correct.

findings.summary: If the owner replies to a review directly on Google, the next poll sets reviews.has_reply=true, but the existing draft stays awaiting_owner/held: it keeps appearing in every daily digest and is marked overdue after 48 hours, and once FR-15 exists an approval would replace the owner's own Google reply. Flow 3 step 5 says a draft stays until the owner acts; the SPEC does not say whether replying on Google counts. The low-rating alert already treats such a review as answered. Recommend a rule (for example: mark such drafts superseded and drop them from the digest).

FR-24 and Flow 0 say nothing is imported or sent while a business is in onboarding. pollReviews reads reviews for onboarding businesses and the owner emails go to them (only offboarded is excluded). Flow 1 connects Google and checks the inbox during onboarding, so reading reviews looks intended, but the SPEC does not say whether owner digest and low-rating emails count as 'sent'. Related to A-6 (an unverified self-signup owner_email would receive them).

The low-rating query does a NOT EXISTS against audit_log by entity/entity_id/action; audit_log is indexed only on (location_id, at) and gets a row per location per poll (96 a day). Not measured; fine at pilot scale. Consider an index on (entity, entity_id, action) when owner emails run on a schedule.

The low-rating idempotency key is the sorted review IDs cut to 256 characters (about 7 UUIDs). If a send's outcome is lost and new low-rated reviews arrive within 24 hours, the retry can reuse the earlier key with a different body; Resend answers 409, which resend.ts retries, so that location's alert keeps failing until the key expires. Rare; not reproduced against Resend.

A 401 from the reviews list with a freshly minted access token (the refresh token itself still worked) is reported as token_revoked, so poll marks the token refresh_failed and stops polling until someone reconnects. Google normally signals scope or permission problems with 403, so this is unlikely; not checked against the real API (no outside accounts allowed).

For reviews Google auto-translates, the v4 comment field can hold '(Translated by Google) ... (Original) ...'. poll stores it as-is and leaves reviews.language null, so the draft (FR-12, rule 1: reply in the review's language) relies on the model picking the original language. Needs a check against a real profile.

SPEC Provider notes: 'no other endpoint is called anywhere; a test fails the build if another Google method is called'. businessProfile.test.ts checks only that module's own calls. A repo-wide check (no file other than src/google/businessProfile.ts references mybusiness*.googleapis.com or businessprofile*.googleapis.com) would enforce 'anywhere'. No violation exists today (grep: only businessProfile.ts and the Sheets reader, which uses the Sheets API).

findings.summary: #33 adds a public waitlist (waitlist_entries: name, business name, email, Google Maps link, business kind; operator notice email). The SPEC's Scope, Data model and retention rules do not mention a waitlist, so the table has no stated retention or deletion rule (Security: collect the minimum personal data; retention rules cover customers only). Recommend adding waitlist_entries to the Data model with a retention period, and the landing page waitlist to Scope. Doc and docs/SPEC.md both need the edit.
